guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 for user-owned and group-owned applications, with authorization and token endpoints. The least-privilege documented scope that covers reading issue titles through the API is read_api, which grants read access to the API including all groups and projects. The api scope is complete read/write and is not selected. Pagination and the specific issues endpoint are not described in the supplied snapshots, so they remain unverified. Access tokens expire after two hours by default and can be refreshed with a refresh token. Setup and execution are untested.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in projects the connected person can access, including paginated results. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Use GitLab OAuth 2 with user-owned or group-owned applications for customer accounts
findings.detail: GitLab can be used as an OAuth 2 identity provider by adding an OAuth 2 application to an instance. Applications can be user-owned or group-owned, and after an application is created, external services can manage access tokens using the OAuth 2 API.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to individual customer accounts connecting through OAuth; each connecting customer organization or workspace authorizes its own account.
